record.title: The Guardian
record.premise: The player sets the three seal-stones in the Kings' Gate, goes through, and kills the Root's guardian, an ancient venomous hydra, alone or with Cuts-the-Old-Knot beside them.
record.foundation: Written 2026-11-17 from main-plot.md quest 18 and §7. Setting the stones (a use of the gate with all three held) opens it and takes the stones into its sockets. Going through the open gate (a use of the gate as a door, which loads the hall) is the stage that, if she was believed, switches Cuts-the-Old-Knot off at the gate and on in the hall while the game loads it (§7); she is never seen to move. The hydra fights in phases (the mod's own); its death ends the quest and MN19 marks the door at the hall's far end. Who must live: nobody (Cuts-the-Old-Knot may die in the fight; the endings read her alive or dead), named in review.

record.title: No Name on the Work Roll
record.premise: A stranger sent up the river on an Owing barge gives the gang's cook their name and trade in the barge's hold, and is freed on the landing by a sour gang-master on an order from Vosh-Leera of Jal-Veesa.
record.foundation: Built from main-plot.md §5 quest 1 (passed by the owner, 2026-11-17) and §1. The game opens in the hold of the Owing barge moored at Ashgate Landing; the hold's door is locked. Okeeh, the gang's cook, asks the player's name (the "player's name set from a conversation" block: the stage after her line opens the game's own name entry) and their trade (a profession as in Morrowind: each answer sets a stage that raises five skills by five; one answer lets the player name their own five, one at a time, each pick a stage that raises that skill by five). When the trade is given the door is unlocked from outside. Dralin Uveran, the gang-master, speaks first on the landing (the quest's one speaks-first line), says the player's name was struck from his roll this morning on Vosh-Leera's order, and passes on her word: she will have work for the player if they bring her some Sithis' beard from Reed-Sill Weir (owner, 2026-11-18: one place at a time, the moss first, then Vosh-Leera). The player's pack holds two lockpicks. MN02 starts on this quest's stage 90 and carries the markers on the weir's moss and on Vosh-Leera's door. The side quest What the Herald Sent is left out: the main quest only. Okeeh and Dralin first answer the line's shared topics Hist, Jal-Veesa and the Owing.

Weeltul, Jal-Veesa's tree-minder, needs Sithis' beard, a grey moss that hangs over the creek below Reed-Sill Weir, to warm her sick tree's cooling egg-pool. Vosh-Leera, who chose the stranger off the barge's list, left word with Dralin that she will have work for the stranger if they bring the moss, for she gives work only to one who helps the tree-minder first.

facts.claim: The player is in the hold of an Owing barge moored at Ashgate Landing, a reed-cutters' camp on the river west of Loriasel, in Black Marsh.
The Owing is the marsh's sentence: months of owed work in place of a cell. The gang is here to serve its months cutting reed.
The hold's door is locked from outside until the gang-master takes the new gang's names.
The player's name was struck from the gang-master's roll this morning, on an order brought by Vosh-Leera, the root-herald of Jal-Veesa: they owe no months and are free.
Vosh-Leera's house is in Jal-Veesa, a town up the road to the east, past Reed-Sill Weir.
Vosh-Leera will have work for the player if they bring her Sithis' beard, a grey moss hanging over the creek below Reed-Sill Weir, which is on the road to the town.
A Hist is a great thinking tree, the size of a tower, with pale grey bark, roots standing out of the water and a pool of eggs at its foot; every Argonian village is built round one.

stages.journalText: Dralin Uveran, the Dunmer gang-master of Ashgate Landing, met me on the landing. He struck my name from his roll this morning, on an order brought by Vosh-Leera, the root-herald of Jal-Veesa, so I owe no months. He does not know why she wants me, and he is sour about it. He says she will have work for me if I bring her some Sithis' beard, a grey moss that hangs over the creek below Reed-Sill Weir, east up the road. I should pick the moss first, then take it to her house in Jal-Veesa, past the weir.
stages.directions: Reed-Sill Weir is the first camp on the road east from the camp's gate, where the road meets the creek, a short walk away; Jal-Veesa is a little further on past the weir.

topics.label: Where am I?
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: "You're in the hold of the work barge, moored at Ashgate Landing, a reed-cutters' camp on the river west of Loriasel. This is Black Marsh, the Argonians' country." The barge brought this gang up from the sea to serve the Owing: months of owed work given by the marsh in place of a cell, served here cutting reed for the mat-makers of Stormhold. She is Okeeh, the gang's cook. The door is locked from outside, as it is for every new gang, until the gang-master, a Dunmer named Dralin Uveran, takes their names onto his roll; it will not be long. She does not know the player's face, and asks their name (a question; its answer is topic.mn01-name). Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: My name? I'll tell you.
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: she listens and says the name back, so she can shout it at mealtimes. Does: sets stage 20, whose start opens the game's name entry; then she asks what the player did before the marsh caught them: "Every gang has a fighter, a hunter, a thief and someone who knows a poultice. What were you?" (a question; its answers are the seven trade topics). Checks: nothing.

topics.label: What do you mean, my trade?
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: what the player did before is what they will be good at here; she lists the answers she has heard and what each is good for: a warrior (One-Handed, Two-Handed, Block, Heavy Armor, Smithing), a hunter (Archery, Sneak, Light Armor, Alchemy, One-Handed), a thief (Sneak, Lockpicking, Pickpocket, Speech, Light Armor), a battlemage (Destruction, Alteration, Conjuration, One-Handed, Heavy Armor), a healer (Restoration, Alchemy, Illusion, Alteration, Speech), a nightblade (Illusion, Sneak, One-Handed, Destruction, Light Armor), or "none of those: name me your own five". Whatever the player says, those five come a little easier from today. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is the Owing?
topics.intent: Okeeh (and, by his own row, Dralin from stage 90). Tells: the Owing is the marsh's sentence. Black Marsh's own towns keep no jails; a debtor, a thief or a stranger who broke the peace is given months of owed work instead, and a broker sells those months to a gang-master like Dralin, who feeds the gang and works them until the months are served. Most of this gang owe six months or a year. Nobody counts a stranger's months kindly. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is the Owing?
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: months of work owed instead of a cell; he buys them from the broker at Stormhold and his cutters work them off on the reed beds. The player's months were bought and are gone now, and that is his loss, not theirs. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is a Hist?
topics.intent: Okeeh, an Argonian. Tells: a Hist is one of the great trees of Black Marsh, and they think. A Hist is as tall as a tower, with pale grey bark and roots standing up out of the water, and a pool at its foot where the eggs lie among the roots. Every Argonian village is built round its own tree. On a hatchling's naming day it licks its tree's sap, and the sap shapes it for life; her own tree is far to the south, and she still dreams of it. All the trees are joined at the root, so what one knows the others can know. An Argonian with a hand on the bark can hear them. They are not just trees: if a village's tree dies, no egg in its pools will hatch again. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is a Hist?
topics.intent: Dralin, a Dunmer. Tells: the Argonians' great trees, grey-barked and as big as towers, with an egg-pool at the foot; every village stands round one, and they say the trees think. He has seen men stand with a hand on one for an hour. Jal-Veesa's is the tall grey tree in the pool at the middle of the town, and it has looked poorly since the rains. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is Jal-Veesa?
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: the town of the Veesa-Teeleel, the Sedge-Wardens, east up the road: stilt houses on mud banks round a pool, boat-lanes cut through the sedge, mats and fish drying on racks. The tall grey tree standing in the pool at the middle of the town is its Hist. She buys the gang's dried fish there. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is Jal-Veesa?
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: the Sedge-Wardens' town, east up the road past Reed-Sill Weir: stilt houses round a pool with their Hist in the middle. Its elders answer to nobody in Stormhold, and its root-herald, Vosh-Leera, speaks for them to outsiders. Her house is in the town; any warden will point to it. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: the gang's cook; she owes no months, she is paid, and she has cooked for Dralin's gangs four seasons. She sells dried fish and lamp oil from her stall by the hut. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Hara-Jeel. Tells: a reed-cutter of this gang, owing a year for a debt at Stormhold; he came up on the barge beside the player and does not know them either. The door opens when the gang-master wants it to. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: (speaks first) You. Off the barge.
topics.intent: Dralin Uveran, a step from the hold's door as the player comes out. Tells: he is Dralin Uveran, gang-master here. Heem-Jasa said I can go at them, shoot them from the reeds, or creep round to the hide's open side unseen; the hide has no door or lock, and if they see me they will fight.

record.title: The Sap Camp
record.premise: At the Naga camp where the sap goes, the player frees Sesk from her cage and hears the names of the Unbound and Cuts-the-Old-Knot; Vosh-Leera sends them by the rootworm to the order's handler in Helstrom.
record.foundation: Built from main-plot.md §5 quest 4. Starts on any of MN03's complete endings (90, 91, 92), all of which leave the player holding the note that names Karsh-Naal Camp; this quest's first stage marks the camp on the map. Sesk is caged at the camp's edge (Skyrim's cage door, placed, Novice lock); its key is on Jeeta-Sakka, the guard who stands at the fire with three others, away from the cage. The player picks the cage, lifts the key or kills the guards; opening the cage door (a use hook) moves the quest. Sesk names the Unbound and Cuts-the-Old-Knot, says the sap is for a draught that has something to do with "the Eye", and calls the grey paste "the seal". Back in Jal-Veesa Vosh-Leera sends the player to the order's handler in Helstrom and pays 100 gold; Weeltul, at the Hist pool, explains the rootworm and its 25-gold fare, and the quest ends there; MN05 carries the ride and the handler's house. The fare is taken by the rootworm stop's own travel line (the tree-minder is the stop's operator; tools/places/build.py plan_travel writes the line and TIF_ARG_BoatTravel removes the fare), so this record only states it. Sesk leaves the camp; the ending switches her off there and on at Helstrom's city landing, where she waits for a raft down the river and owes the player (her side quest, main-plot §6, hangs on that line).

She is sending me to the order's handler, Nesh-Deeka, at her house in Helstrom, far to the south through deadly country. She told me to ride the rootworm: a great blind worm that swims the waters under the roots from one Hist's pool to another's. It stops at a tree's root pool, the open water among the roots at its foot, where a root-tender calls it and takes the fare. Here the tender is Weeltul, at the Hist pool in the middle of the town, and the fare is twenty-five gold. I should ask her to send me.

The jars come here and go on to Cuts-the-Old-Knot. The sap is for a draught she brews, and the draught is for something to do with "the Eye"; Sesk never learned what. topics.label: Who is Cuts-the-Old-Knot?
topics.intent: Sesk. Tells: the Unbound's leader. Sesk saw her once: an Argonian woman, thin, quiet, who looked at the trees as if they had wronged her. She never stays where her crews are. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.intent: Sesk. Tells: the grey paste the crews press into a scar after they drain it; the cut closes over it. It comes in bottles from Cuts-the-Old-Knot's people. Sesk does not know what is in it or why they use it. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: I found where the sap goes.
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera. Tells: she hears it all: the Unbound, Cuts-the-Old-Knot, a draught, "the Eye", the seal. This is more than a herald can judge. The road there runs through deadly country, so the player is to ride the rootworm, and she tells them what it is: a great blind worm that swims the waters under the roots from one Hist's pool to another's, faster than any boat. It stops at a tree's root pool, the open water among the roots at the tree's foot, where a root-tender calls it with a hand on the bark and takes the fare. Here the root-tender is Weeltul, at the Hist pool in the middle of the town; the fare is twenty-five gold. At Helstrom it comes up in the pool under the city tree, and the root-tender there can point the way to Nesh-Deeka's House. She pays the player a hundred gold. record.title: The Handler
record.premise: In Helstrom the order's handler hears what the player found, has them win a jar of stolen sap off an Unbound go-between, makes them a Voh-Vastei and sends them after an "Eye of Argonia" for sale in Gideon.
sources: story/design/quests/lines/main-plot.md §3 §4 §5 quest 5 and the rank table §9
record.foundation: Built from main-plot.md §5 quest 5 and the rank table. The player rides the rootworm from Jal-Veesa's pool (the travel network's fare line, 25 gold) to Helstrom's city tree, where Cheeval-Xu works the rootworm, and finds Nesh-Deeka's House, one of the city's one-room Argonian houses, its door showing her name. Nesh-Deeka hears the report and tells the player what the Eye of Argonia is and where it lies; the player says what the draught must be for and she agrees. To prove the player she sends them for a jar of stolen sap kept by Keel-Raa, an Unbound go-between who lodges at the Boatmen's Lodge (Helstrom's inn, a ship's hold interior kept by Sleeps-Last) with two hired men beside him, none hostile, in a band of ours whose members' wrongs Helstrom's levy does not punish (Skyrim's flag that reports no crimes against its members). The jar is in his pack, a knapsack on the crates behind the three. The player lifts it from the pack unseen (Sneak), buys it for 100 gold (he gives the player the pack, and so the one jar in it), or fights the three for it. On the jar's hand-in Nesh-Deeka makes the player a Voh-Vastei (the rank, Sign of Cipactli's light Argonian armour under our name, the order's traders and 200 gold), gives the order's aim and her one lead, an "Eye of Argonia" for sale in Gideon, by the rootworm from Helstrom's city tree: stage 90, which starts MN06. record.title: The Grey Tooth
record.premise: The Toh-Reel-Ka's new Toh-Wo follows the parchment map to the Grey Tooth on Skeith Isle, gets past the Collector's men to learn the kings' stone was carried off to the Stormwidow, takes it from under the Unbound scouts in the beached wreck's hold, hears a wounded scout's word about the cellar of Fort Chalkmoth, and brings the stone to Never-Writes-Twice.
record.foundation: Built from the main plot (story/design/quests/lines/main-plot.md §5 quest 11, passed by the owner), and invents nothing it does not give beyond the names listed in the review (L8). The quest starts on MN10's last stage (90, its completed ending): Never-Writes-Twice, now the player's officer at the back of Nesh-Deeka's House in Helstrom, has read the parchment map and marked the Grey Tooth. It uses the crag's small cave on the north face and the Stormwidow's sand-filled hold only; the cairn, its cache and the stern's strongbox belong to Bramman's Brethren and are never named as targets. The Collector's three hired men at the foot of the goat-path and in the cave, and the three Unbound scouts and the wounded scout at the wreck, are switched on by stage 10's start (the player is in Helstrom, another cell far away), so a player of the Brethren's line who comes first meets neither. Each step is a thing read or taken or a line picked: reading the Collector's rubbing moves the player on to the wreck; taking the marker stone moves them to the wounded scout; her words (or, if she is dead, the scrap of bark she carried) move them to the report; Never-Writes-Twice's report line completes the quest, which starts MN12 (the player's own errand to the cellar of Fort Chalkmoth) and MN13 (the hunt: Bell Station) together. The seal's recipe is optional: reading it teaches the poison's ingredients, and three bottles of the poison lie with it. Who the quest cannot go on without: Never-Writes-Twice.

truth.what: The captain of the Stormwidow, a ship of Bramman's Brethren, found a carved stone of the old kings in a niche of the cave and had it carried aboard. His men scratched on the niche's lintel in Cyrodilic that the stone went to the Stormwidow by her captain's order. Weeks later the Archwardens' privateers ran the ship onto Skeith Isle's south-west beach and killed her crew (the wreck's place history).

The Collector, who hunts the Eye, sent hired men to dig the cave. They found the empty niche. Vanin took a rubbing of the lintel's scratch, wrote his own lines under it and left it in the cave for his men, then sold the wreck's name to the Unbound for gold (plot §4, the Collector tells what he learns to whoever pays). His men still dig in case the stone came back.

Unbound scouts camped in the sand-filled hold and search its ballast crates for the stone. They carry their leader's recipe for the seal and three bottles of it. Tah-Leesh, one of them, fell through a rotten deck onto the beach below the bow, and the others left her there, unable to walk.

Tah-Leesh has heard Cuts-the-Old-Knot say that whoever serves the Toh-Reel-Ka should ask what moans in the cellar of Fort Chalkmoth. She does not know the answer. She scratched the words on a scrap of bark to keep them.

Never-Writes-Twice reads the marker stone's seven towers as the drowned spires off Lilmoth and sends the player to the divers of Bell Station. Asked about Fort Chalkmoth, she says it is a fort like any other. She lies (plot §3).

record.title: The Cellar Door
record.premise: On their own account, the Toh-Wo gets into Fort Chalkmoth's keep by the wall captain's price or by the trapdoor in the yard, finds jars of Jal-Veesa's sap stacked by the stair in the quartermaster's store, faces the order's gaoler in the guardroom, and finds the cellar's inner door locked with moaning behind it and its key not in the fort.
record.foundation: Built from the main plot (§5 quest 12, passed by the owner). The player's own errand, begun by the wounded scout's words and Never-Writes-Twice's answer in MN11; it runs beside MN13 (the hunt) and either may come first. Four steps in the plot's order where it gives one: the way in (the captain's price, or the trapdoor in the yard unseen), then the store, the gaoler and the door, which the player may do in any order once inside, as one working stage (quest-write §3.4) with three objectives. The fort's main source, Fort Neugrad, gives the keep (its Adept lock serves as the store's door) and the prison below it (the cellar), whose passage door is set as the trapdoor in the yard and comes up into the guardroom. The gaoler's test is the "spell cast in front of a person as a test" block (owner, #73), to be proven once; until proven the gate stands in as Illusion 25. The plot has two people speak first (the wall captain at the gate and the gaoler); the ceiling allows one, so the gaoler speaks first (every way in meets him) and the captain stands at the gate with a marker and the objective. The cellar's question stays open: the player learns only that sap from Jal-Veesa is stored by the stair in a fort with no Hist, the gaoler's "they sleep, and they dream", and moaning behind a door whose key is not in the fort. The last stage turns the player back to the hunt: to Bell Station if MN13 is not yet done, to the seal-stones if it is.

topics.label: (speaks first)
topics.intent: Corvus Ulvius, outside the gate. Tells: this is the Rose, and the Blackguards' heirs born in it hold it now; strangers who walk in are killed on the walls. He lets a stranger in as a guest three ways: 300 gold to him, words good enough to move him, or a duel with him, fists and steel, until one yields. A guest walks the yard and the hall and nobody touches them. Anyone who climbs the walls without his leave is fair game, and anyone who kills him has the whole Rose to fight. If the player asks what they want inside, he says the raj-kaal Okaz-Teel keeps the old warden's vault in his hall and the key on his belt, and he already has a buyer for what lies in it, the Imperial in the hall. Offers topic.mn14-toll, topic.mn14-persuade and topic.mn14-duel as answers. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Here is your toll. (300 gold)
topics.intent: Corvus. Checks: goldAtLeast 300. Tells: he waves the player in as a guest of the Rose; the walls will let them be. Does: takes 300 gold; sets stage 20. Fallback: no coin, no gate; words or steel are the other ways.

topics.label: (Persuade) The Toh-Reel-Ka can send you a hundred like me. Let one in quietly instead.
topics.intent: Corvus. Checks: skillAtLeast [Speech, 75]. Tells: he laughs and lets the player in as a guest, since a quiet Reel-Ka is cheaper than a loud one. Does: sets stage 20. Fallback: words are wind at this gate; the player is left the toll or a duel, and this line is not offered again.

topics.label: I'll fight you for the gate.
topics.intent: Corvus. Tells: he likes that; until one of them yields; if he yields, the player walks in as a guest; if the player kills him, the Rose fights them. Does: sets stage 15 (the duel begins, the yield block).

topics.label: (on yielding)
topics.intent: Corvus, when he yields. Tells: enough; he gives the gate; the player is a guest of the Rose and nobody on the walls will touch them. Does: sets flag.mn14.yielded (stage 20).

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Corvus. Tells: captain of the Rose's gate, born in its cells like his father and his father's mother; he keeps the gate because he has not lost a fight at it in eleven years.

topics.label: Who are the Blackguards' heirs?
topics.intent: Corvus. Tells: the Rose was the Empire's prison, built for Argonians; when the Empire left, the prisoners' children took it for their own and call it the Rose; they live by the road and the boat, and they answer to the raj-kaal, Okaz-Teel, a Naga of the deep swamp.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Okaz-Teel, in his hall (talks only to a guest; at 25 a player who speaks to him is seen). Tells: he is the raj-kaal of the Rose, the war-chief of its people; a Naga is an Argonian of the deep swamp, and he says it with pride. The warden's vault in his wall holds a thief's old stone; the Imperial has offered for it and been told to wait; the key is on his belt and goes to whoever pays 1,000 gold first. He watches his own belt, and his people watch the vault, and a thief they see is a thief they kill.

topics.label: I'll buy the key to the warden's vault. (1000 gold)
topics.intent: Okaz-Teel. Checks: goldAtLeast 1000. Tells: the Imperial waited too long; he gives the key and says the stone is the player's. Does: sets stage 22 (takes 1,000 gold, gives the key and the chest's contents). Fallback: 1,000 gold, not a coin less; the Imperial can still outbid a pauper.

topics.label: (greeting)
topics.intent: The Collector, in the hall (he never fights and never calls the guards). Tells: so the Toh-Reel-Ka's hound has found him again; he left the player a note in Gideon; he has offered for the stone and been told to wait, and he will not bid against the order. He has a side errand for a capable hand: a riddle, not a road, and the Eye can wait for it; what lies at the end of it is made for whatever guards the Root. (The side quest itself is its own record.)

topics.label: That ring on your finger. What is it?
topics.intent: The Collector. Tells: Kothringi silver, from a knight's barrow in the Kotherra; it steadies the hand at a lock or a pocket; it is not for sale. If the player asks what he would lose: alive he is worth more to them than the ring, for his errand; a dead man gives no riddles.

topics.label: The Collector
topics.intent: Corvus. Tells: the Imperial paid the toll like an honest man, which nobody here trusts; he sits in the hall as the raj-kaal's guest waiting to buy the stone.

topics.label: Umbriel
topics.intent: Corvus. Tells: the flying city came down on Lilmoth when his grandmother was a girl; its dead came as far as the Rose's walls and the walls held.

topics.label: Remind me what we are hunting, and why.
topics.intent: Never-Writes-Twice, at the back of Nesh-Deekas House. Tells: the Eye of Argonia is the old priest-kings jewel, cut from Hist amber. It sits at the Root, the place under the sea below Teku-Sul Spire where the roots of every Hist meet. Used where it sits, it pours strength down every root and heals every sick tree; lifted from its place, it cuts every tree from every other for good. The last king shut it behind the Kings Gate, which opens only with its three seal-stones: the thiefs stone in Blackrose Prison, the stone in the flooded vaults of Gemin and the stone in the deepest hall of Vorannuhl. A beast guards the Root; Cuts-the-Old-Knot brews a draught from drained sap strong enough to kill it, so she can reach the Eye. The orders aim: take the stones first, open the gate, use the Eye in place to heal the trees, bring the stones back to her so the chamber is sealed for good, and end the Unbound. She looks at the stones the player carries and names the places of those still missing.

The Toh-Reel-Ka are the secret warriors of the Xeech-Leel, the party that rules Black Marsh, made so that no tree could bring another Umbriel. Used where it sits, the Eye heals every tree, and the dreamers see through them all again; lifted, it parts the trees, about three in ten die, and the dreams end. If I fight her, I take her tomes, staff and draughts, face the guardian alone, and cannot give her the Eye. If I believe her, she fights the guardian beside me and giving her the Eye stays open. "How did your handler always know where to send you? Why was there sap in a fort with no tree (the jar of Jal-Veesa sap the player took from the store, thing.mn12.sap-jar)? Who did you think was behind the cellar door? And why did nobody warn you that we were here?" The Toh-Reel-Ka keep people in the cellar of Fort Chalkmoth, feed them sap and make them tell their dreams; a dreamer sees what any tree has seen, anywhere, and through them the order sees the whole marsh. The moans were dreamers. She was one for nine years; Never-Writes-Twice kept the key, and her story that Cuts went mad on sap and killed her minders is a lie. The answer to the player's question: she seals each tree she drains so the order draws no sap from it for its dreamers and its dreamers cannot see her through it; under the sea there are no trees, so nobody saw her here. She never meant a tree to die of her seal, and some have. She grants the order its reason: no second Umbriel, the flying city that the An-Xileel called down on Lilmoth with Lilmoth's mad Hist in 4E 48, whose dead killed the city's people. But the Xeech-Leel, the party that has ruled Black Marsh since the An-Xileel fell and that made the Toh-Reel-Ka, took the marsh by being not the An-Xileel and now rule unseen through the trees as the An-Xileel did. The healing the player was sent to do is for the dreamers: a sick tree shows them nothing, a healed one shows them everything, and the stones "kept safe" mean only the order can ever reach the Eye. She wants the Eye lifted, which parts the trees, ends the dreams and breaks the order; many trees will die of it, with the villages under them, and she will not pretend otherwise. She asks the player to stand with her or fight her here (answers: topic.mn17-fight, topic.mn17-believe). Does: sets stage 30.

topics.label: Tell me about the cellar.
topics.intent: Cuts. Tells: the dreamers lie behind the locked door the player heard; they are given sap each night and asked each morning what they saw; she was there nine years; she found a way out and will not say how, because the way may still serve the others.

topics.label: Why seal a tree you have drained?
topics.intent: Cuts. Tells: so the order gets no sap from it for its dreamers and its dreamers cannot see through it where she goes. The seal is a paralysis poison; it numbs the scar shut. She meant it to close a tree, not kill it, and some have died; she carries that.

topics.label: What does the order really want with the Eye?
topics.intent: Cuts. Tells: every tree healed is a tree their dreamers can see through again; the stones taken home mean nobody but them reaches the Eye after; the Xeech-Leel's rule rests on the dreamers.

topics.label: What happens if the Eye is lifted?
topics.intent: Cuts. Tells: every tree is cut from every other for good; no dreamer sees through them again; the strong trees live alone; the weak die, perhaps three in ten, and their villages with them, because no egg in a dead tree's pool hatches. She thinks a free marsh is worth that. If the player asks about Jal-Veesa's or Teel-Fen's tree, she says she does not know which will die.

topics.label: And if I fight you?
topics.intent: Cuts. Tells: then she drinks the draught she brewed for the guardian and the player will have to kill her; they may take what she carries, her tomes and her staff and the rest of the draught, and face the guardian alone; and the Eye will be theirs to use or lift, never hers.

topics.label: And if I believe you?
topics.intent: Cuts. Tells: she goes through the gate with them when it opens and fights the guardian at their side; she asks for no promise now; at the Eye the choice is theirs, to use it as the order wants, lift it themselves, or let her lift it. If they use it while she lives, the sap she has drunk will carry its power through her, and she knows it.

topics.label: The order sent me to kill you. I will.
topics.intent: Cuts. Tells: then so be it; she drinks. Does: sets stage 40; she turns hostile (speaker_hostile) and drinks her draught.

topics.label: I believe you. Open the gate with me.
topics.intent: Cuts. Tells: then set the stones; she will be at their side beyond the gate. Does: sets stage 90 (flag.mn.cuts-believed).

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Cuts. Tells: she leads the Unbound, the tribeless who belong to no tree's village; her name is the one she gave herself when she got out of the cellar.

topics.label: Umbriel
topics.intent: Cuts. Tells: the An-Xileel spoke alone with Lilmoth's mad tree and brought the city down; the order was made so nobody could do it again, and now the order speaks alone with every tree.

topics.label: Remind me what we are hunting, and why.
topics.intent: Never-Writes-Twice, at the back of Nesh-Deekas House. Tells: the Eye of Argonia is the old priest-kings jewel, cut from Hist amber. It sits at the Root, the place under the sea below Teku-Sul Spire where the roots of every Hist meet. Used where it sits, it pours strength down every root and heals every sick tree; lifted from its place, it cuts every tree from every other for good. The last king shut it behind the Kings Gate, which opens only with its three seal-stones: the thiefs stone in Blackrose Prison, the stone in the flooded vaults of Gemin and the stone in the deepest hall of Vorannuhl. A beast guards the Root; Cuts-the-Old-Knot brews a draught from drained sap strong enough to kill it, so she can reach the Eye. The orders aim: take the stones first, open the gate, use the Eye in place to heal the trees, bring the stones back to her so the chamber is sealed for good, and end the Unbound. She looks at the stones the player carries and names the places of those still missing.
